item.claim: RunSqlTool's execute scope already defines `cap_size` and `row_cap_hit`, and `cap_size` is the row cap in effect for this query, not a fixed 10,000.
DataFrameComponent.from_records accepts a `data=` keyword and stores it on the component's `data` attribute, which row_cap_of reads.
RunSqlTool has a `self.dialect` attribute that is set from its constructor's `dialect=` argument.
run_sql.py imports sqllens._table_payload, which imports sqllens.agent.markers and sqllens.safety.readonly; no import cycle when sqllens.agent loads first.
The DataFrameComponent handed to run_sql_display_line holds the same rows the formatter later receives via ui_component.rich_component, so N matches the block's row_count.
is_introspection_query takes a `dialect=` keyword and returns False on unparseable SQL; other parser errors propagate and are caught by the broad except in run_sql_display_line.

The `_undisplayable_result_text` candidate sits in the branch taken when _build_table_payload returns None (headers over 130 KB or build failure); last_sql_is_introspection is correct there; a result_text candidate is emitted as a text block at the result's position in blocks and Markdown.
For a one-row short-text result, the payload passed to _small_result_to_markdown is the table payload from _compute_table_payload, so it carries row_cap when the marker is set.
row_cap in table blocks survives copy/sanitize steps (copy_bounded_json, 512 KB trim) between _compute_table_payload and the emitted block.
The widget reads block.row_cap, block.row_count and block.truncated with the same key names the Python payload emits.
--fg and --accent CSS variables are defined in the widget theme, so .cutnotice gets normal text colour and an accent border.
The buildCsvExport warning string is displayed to the user by the export handler, and rows.length is the count of data rows in the exported file.
The test stub `const csvCutWarning=()=>""` is enough for the regex-extracted buildCsvExport; the extracted functions do not need state.truncated, fmtCount or capSentence.
The _Ctx, _StaticRunner and _NoopFileSystem fakes match the interfaces RunSqlTool.execute uses.
mark_truncation(df, truncated=..., max_rows=...) exists with those keywords and sets the attrs RunSqlTool reads into row_cap_hit/cap_size.
The "Result truncated at 300 rows" text the test asserts matches the existing truncation_note wording in run_sql.py.
Monkeypatching _compute_table_payload on sqllens.tools._format takes effect because _build_table_payload looks the name up in _format's namespace.
In tests/unit/test_format.py, helpers _ui, _sql_card(sql, status=...), _MAX_ROWS_RENDERED, _serialized_len and _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES are imported/defined.

AC1: display-cut notice 'Showing the first N of M rows. The other K rows were left out to fit the display size limit.' above the bar, fg colour, 3px accent left border, wraps; meta reads 'showing X of N' with no truncated suffix.
AC2: capped table shows 'The query stopped at the cap-row limit; more rows exist.' with the cap in effect; both limits share one line, display sentence first.
AC3: a table cut by neither limit shows no notice in the widget and no new Markdown note.
AC4: Markdown display-cut note states R=min(N,500), M and K, plus 'lists at most 500 rows' when R<N; replaces the 500 footer; part of the table's Markdown; holds at M<=500 and R<500<M.
AC5: in Markdown, the row-cap sentence comes directly under the table, after the display note or the 500 footer.
AC6: a one-row short-text result whose query hit the cap ends its text block with the cap sentence.

AC7: a non-empty non-schema-lookup result with no table block yields at its position in blocks and Markdown 'The query returned M rows that could not be displayed.', plus the cap sentence when capped.
AC8: hidden schema-lookup result gets no block, notice or display line; uses is_introspection_query with configured dialect; unparseable SQL counts as a data query.
AC9: every number in widget notice, Markdown notes and CSV warning uses comma thousands separators.

AC10: CSV warning on display-cut table reads 'Warning: this CSV holds only the C rows shown, not all M.'; on capped table states C rows shown and query stopped at cap; formula warning still alongside.
AC11: table blocks carry row_cap when capped; row_count+truncated equals rows returned; every block without type key, row_cap included, serializes to at most _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES.

AC12: when the table will be cut, the agent's tool result states M and that the table shows only the first N, N equal to the formatter's row_count; headers-too-large case says the M rows are too large to show as a table.
AC13: if the schema-lookup check or size calculation raises inside run_sql, the query still succeeds with today's result (no display line) and a WARNING is logged.

AC14: system prompt has no full/complete wording about result tables (per-region example reworded); carries cut-table and row-cap answer rule scoped to emit_text or final reply, never-full/complete rule incl. introductions, no-schema-lookup rule, clarifying-question precedence.

AC15: the agent is told the widget's N; only the Markdown note states the smaller 500 count; an uncut result longer than 500 rows keeps the 'Showing first 500 of M rows' footer and sends no display line.
AC16: chart truncation display, 512 KB trim notice, no-download behaviour and the formatter's unguarded is_introspection_query call are unchanged.
test_widget_export_outcomes exports FAKES, NODE, _between and _run_js with the call shapes used here.
The FAKES DOM supports the DOM APIs the test and renderTableBlock use.
query_results.html contains the '// ───────────────────────────── chart block' marker after renderTableBlock, and the extracted text is self-contained apart from host, clip, PAGE_SIZE and flashMeta.
renderTableBlock returns a container whose first child holds the cut notice (class cutnotice) and second the bar (class bar) with a meta span.
The CSV export section defines buildCsvExport() returning an object with .warning, depending only on state, sortedRows, filteredRows, render, gridHost and metaSpan.
The renderTableBlock start marker exists in the widget
The table block fixture keys columns, rows, row_count, truncated and optional row_cap match the server's table block.
The CSV state fixture keys columns, rows, rowCount, truncated and rowCap match the widget state built from a block; rowCap 0 means cap not hit.
The FORMULA constant exactly matches the existing formula-protection warning text in the widget

The changelog says, with no qualifier, that a result too large to show as a table now produces a text block saying the rows could not be displayed. This would fail for a non-empty data-query result in any path where no table block is emitted and the candidate is never added, for example when the table-payload build raises instead of returning None.
